items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Did you ever think of Faith Marables banjo player's name... [INTERVIEWEE] I don't know his name.

ctx.x: That's right. My old sister. Yeah, that was in the Tampa roof guard.
Yeah, I see. Did you ever think of Faith Marables banjo player's name, that little bright fellow that went to penitentiary? Oh, yeah, that boy, no.

I don't know his name. Uh-uh. Now, you know who could tell you his name? Sales. Yeah, I didn't say I was going to tell you his name. Okay. Maybe George Gano, but I'm most sure if Sales could. I'll ask Sales when he comes back. Yeah, I'll ask Sales. I'm most sure he could tell you. Yeah. Uh-huh. Now, that Raymond Brown senior, the daddy, he was the drumroll player and the son? Yeah, yeah. Son played trumpet. I played with him on the Pelican, with Pichon's band. Oh, yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: Sometime they'd hire Faith Marable. He had his band up there. ... Fine band. Who was with Faith about that time? ... Well, I never met him.

ctx.x: Yeah, very awesome. 35, Rampart and Girard. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

Then we had, uh, Dandy Lewis on bass. You heard of him. Yeah, I've heard Bess talk about him. That's right. Dandy Lewis. That's who we had on bass. Then after Buddy Johnson left, we taken Earl Umphrey on trombone. He played up there with us. Then... Manny Mineta come up there with us a while. Yeah, he told us he did. Yeah, he come up. He played with us a while. We had a nice band. Five band. We used to have two bands. Celestine, our band, and they had the big carnival bars. They hired two bands. Sometime they'd…
Something like that? Or was it Lawson?
